extracted.intended_audience: law students, legal scholars, university administrators, and lawyers interested in legal education/history
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and institutional rules governing the introduction and regulation of instruction in the laws of England at Oxford (Mr Viner's benefaction and the resulting statutes), together with arguments about the propriety and benefits of teaching common law in universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of common law knowledge for civilians and canonists
rubrics_metrics.description: Every civilian and canonist that would act with safety as a judge, or with prudence and reputation as an advocate, must know in what cases and how far the English laws have given sanction to the Roman; in what points the latter are rejected; and where they are intermixed and blended together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as an imperative for practitioners to avoid error and to act prudently; it motivates including municipal law in academical study so jurists know differences between domestic and civil/canon law.

rubrics_metrics.name: University requirement for common law inquiry (Oxford statute)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the three questions to be annually discussed at the act by the jurist-inceptors shall relate to the common law; subjoining this reason: 'quia juris civilis studiosos decet haud imperitos esse juris municipalis, & differentias exteri patriique juris notas habere.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses a formal expectation within university procedure that students of civil law be conversant with municipal (common) law differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of universities to teach laws of the land
rubrics_metrics.description: The universities are proper places to afford instruction in the laws of the land to gentlemen of all ranks and degrees; such study will not obstruct other pursuits and will ornament and assist them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argumentative criterion: universities provide association with peers, wise disciplining, and time to study law without interfering with gentlemanly pursuits; thus law is fit for academical instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law as an academical subject (ethical/pedagogical criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A science which distinguishes right and wrong, employs the noblest faculties, and is universal in use and extent (i.e., jurisprudence) is fit to be studied in a university and is the principal branch of ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifies inclusion of law among university sciences on intellectual and moral grounds; useful when deciding curricular scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate accounts and annual audit of benefaction
rubrics_metrics.description: That the accounts of this benefaction be separately kept, and annually audited by the delegates of accounts and professor, and afterwards reported to convocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial oversight requirement for institutional endowments; ensures transparency and reporting to university governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and qualifications for the Professorship of the Laws of England
rubrics_metrics.description: That a professorship of the laws of England be established, with a salary of two hundred pounds per annum; the professor to be elected by convocation, and to be at the time of his election at least a master of arts or bachelor of civil law in the university of Oxford, of ten years standing from his matriculation; and also a barrister at law of four years standing at the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets formal eligibility and election procedure for the chair; combines university degree seniority and practical professional standing as prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professor's required public and yearly lectures; language and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: That such professor (by himself, or by deputy...) do read one solemn public lecture on the laws of England, and in the English language, in every academical term, at certain stated times previous to the commencement of the common law term; or forfeit twenty pounds for every omission to Mr Viner's general fund: and also (by himself, or by deputy...) do yearly read one complete course of lectures on the laws of England, and in the English language, consisting of sixty lectures at the least, to be read during the university term time, with such proper intervals that not more than four lectures may fall within any single week: that the professor do give a month's notice of the time when the course is to begin, and do read gratis to the scholars of Mr Viner's foundation; but may demand of other auditors such gratuity as shall be settled from time to time by decree of convocation: and that, for every of the said sixty lectures omitted, the professor, on complaint made to the vice-chancellor within the year, do forfeit forty shillings to Mr Viner's general fund; the proof of having performed his duty to lie upon the said professor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed teaching obligations: language (English), minimum counts (one solemn per term; 60 lectures/year), scheduling limits (≤4 lectures/week), notice requirements, preferential free access for foundation scholars, ability to charge other auditors, and specified financial penalties with burden of proof on professor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and use of deputies for lectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Professor may read by deputy, but deputies (if occasional) must be previously approved by convocation (or by vice-chancellor and proctors), or, if permanent, both the cause and the deputy to be annually approved by convocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls delegation of teaching duties to ensure oversight and university approval of substitutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professor tenure and grounds for removal
rubrics_metrics.description: That every professor do continue in his office during life, unless in case of such misbehaviour as shall amount to bannition by the university statutes; or unless he deserts the profession of the law by betaking himself to another profession; or unless, after one admonition by the vice-chancellor and proctors for notorious neglect, he is guilty of another flagrant omission: in any of which cases he be deprived by the vice-chancellor, with consent of the house of convocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies life tenure subject to deprivation for gross misconduct, change of profession, or repeated neglect despite admonition; places removal power with vice-chancellor and convocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and terms of fellowships and scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: That such a number of fellowships with a stipend of fifty pounds per annum, and scholarships with a stipend of thirty pounds be established, as the convocation shall from time to time ordain, according to the state of Mr Viner's revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies funding amounts and that quantity/creation is subject to convocation's determination based on endowment resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and election criteria for fellows and scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: That every fellow be elected by convocation, and at the time of election be unmarried, and at least a master of arts or bachelor of civil law, and a member of some college or hall in the university of Oxford; the scholars of this foundation or such as have been scholars (if qualified and approved of by convocation) to have the preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets marital status, degree, and college membership as eligibility requirements and provides selection preference to foundation scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations for fellows (call to bar and residence)
rubrics_metrics.description: That, if not a barrister when chosen, he be called to the bar within one year after his election; but do reside in the university two months in every year, or in case of non-residence do forfeit the stipend of that year to Mr Viner's general fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes professional advancement (call to bar) within a time limit and annual residence obligations, with financial forfeiture for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholars' matriculation, lecture attendance, degree, call to bar, and residence conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: That every scholar be elected by convocation, and at the time of election be unmarried, and a member of some college or hall in the university, who shall have been matriculated twenty four calendar months at the least: that he do take the degree of bachelor of civil law with all convenient speed; (either proceeding in arts or otherwise) and previous to his taking the same, between the second and eighth year from his matriculation, be bound to attend two courses of the professor's lectures, to be certified under the professor's hand; and within one year after taking the same be called to the bar: that he do annually reside six months till he is of four years standing, and four months from that time till he is master of arts or bachelor of civil law; after which he be bound to reside two months in every year; or, in case of non-residence, do forfeit the stipend of that year to Mr Viner's general fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive scholar obligations: minimum matriculation duration, mandatory lecture attendance (two courses between years 2–8, certified), degree requirement (BCL), call to bar within one year of degree, graduated residence requirements tied to years of standing, and forfeiture for non-residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voi(d)ing and forfeiture conditions for scholarships and fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: That the scholarships do become void in case of non-attendance on the professor, or not taking the degree of bachelor of civil law, being duly admonished so to do by the vice-chancellor and proctors: and that both fellowships and scholarships do expire at the end of ten years after each respective election; and become void in case of gross misbehaviour, non-residence for two years together, marriage, not being called to the bar within the time before limited, (being duly admonished so to be by the vice-chancellor and proctors) or deserting the profession of the law by following any other profession: and that in any of these cases the vice-chancellor, with consent of convocation, do declare the place actually void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates multiple disqualifying events (non-attendance, failure to take BCL after admonition, gross misbehaviour, prolonged non-residence, marriage, failure to be called to bar, desertion of profession) and a fixed ten-year maximum tenure; provides procedure for declaring vacancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure on vacancy and timing of elections
rubrics_metrics.description: That in case of any vacancy of the professorship, fellowships, or scholarships, the profits of the current year be ratably divided between the predecessor or his representatives, and the successor; and that a new election be had within one month afterwards, unless by that means the time of election shall fall within any vacation, in which case it be deferred to the first week in the next full term. And that before any convocation shall be held for such election, or for any other matter relating to Mr Viner's benefaction, ten days public notice be given to each college and hall of the convocation, and the cause of convoking it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies transitional financial allocation, a tight timetable for replacement elections with a vacation exception, and a 10-day public notice requirement prior to convocation relating to the benefaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and form requirements for teaching common law
rubrics_metrics.description: Lectures and courses on the laws of England to be read in the English language (explicit requirement in the statutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes accessibility and vernacular instruction; linked to requirement of a 'solemn public lecture... in the English language' and entire yearly course likewise in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching load scheduling constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: The yearly course of sixty lectures to be read during the university term time, with such proper intervals that not more than four lectures may fall within any single week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a pacing requirement to distribute lectures reasonably across term time rather than concentrating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities' potential scholarly role in improving law
rubrics_metrics.description: The leisure and abilities of the learned in university retirements might suggest expedients or execute reforms for improving the method of the law, retrenching superfluities, and reconciling contrarieties created by long practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets an expectation (normative) that university-based scholarship should engage in methodical improvement and rationalization of legal doctrine — a criterion for academic contribution to the profession.
